properties.Location: South Side of Santa Rosa Island, Between Ford Point and South Point
properties.IncidentOverview: Current Situation – May 21; 2026 Overnight; fire activity was significantly lower compared to previous nights. Though crews continued to observe active burning along the northernmost section near Telephone Road and south of Soledad Peak; activity was mostly limited to low-intensity ground fire and smoldering; and no new heat was detected. Relative humidity levels at Black Mountain remained much higher than earlier in the week; hovering around 50% overnight—a significant change from Wednesday morning; when humidity averaged near 15%. Channel Islands National Park’s Landing Craft – the Surf Ranger - left before dark at 4:30 AM this morning to bring additional equipment out to the island. Supply boats and passenger boats continue to make trips to the island daily to provide logistical support for firefighting efforts and transport personnel to and from the incident. Today; firefighters on the western side of the incident will concentrate their efforts in the Cloud Forest area along Main (Soledad) Road working south toward the South Point Spur and the South Point Lighthouse. On the eastern flank; the fire has passed through the Water Canyon Campground but the campground itself remains in good condition overall. The only damage reported was the loss of one wind barrier structure. These V-shaped wooden wind fences are installed at campsites to help shield campers from the strong winds that funnel through Water Canyon. No other major campground infrastructure was lost. Firefighters are using direct suppression tactics on the Telephone Road Trail just north of the campground to stop the fire’s forward progress. Additionally; crews will progress from Soledad Peak eastward along Main (Soledad) Road; monitoring the existing containment line to ensure it continues to hold; and taking action on any new heat if found. They will also construct additional line along Telephone Road and north into Cherry Canyon. Resource Advisors continue working alongside firefighters to ensure that sensitive species and the island’s cultural assets are accommodated as effectively as possible throughout firefighting operations. As fire activity is diminishing; Resource Advisors will begin to discuss suppression repair. Suppression repair refers to the immediate post-fire actions taken to repair impacts caused by firefighting activities and to minimize secondary environmental effects such as soil erosion; water quality degradation; and habitat loss. Background: On Friday; May 15; 2026; an aircraft flying over Santa Rosa Island in Channel Islands National Park reported a wildfire. National Park Service (NPS) staff already on the island confirmed it later that morning. The Santa Rosa Island Fire is located on the southeastern end of the island in remote and rugged terrain. This is a full-suppression human-caused wildfire and is under investigation. Closures: The National Park Service has closed Santa Rosa Island to day use and overnight use at least through this week due to the wildfire. Visitors with campground reservations at Water Canyon Campground have been notified via e-mail. Structures: There are two uninhabited historic structures in the area; Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed on the western edge; and Wreck Line Camp Cabin on the eastern edge. Unfortunately; both have been confirmed destroyed. An additional storage structure was also destroyed adjacent to Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed.
